title: Man. Post. Cap. X: PLAC third — sin is not imputed when there is no law; no law for Adam’s act
pass_a_gloss: Third argument from what follows: sin is not imputed when there is no law. But there is no law by which Adam’s actual sin is imputed to us. Therefore it is not imputed. The major is Paul’s. If any such law existed, it was the singular ban on the tree of knowledge. That ban has not existed for millennia—the tree gone from nature, or wholly unknown to us and granted like other creatures. So no such law remains.
pass_b_english: A third argument is supplied to me by what follows in the Apostle: sin is not imputed when there is no law.
But there is no law according to which Adam’s actual sin is imputed to us.
Therefore it is not imputed to us.
I prove the minor: for the major is the Apostle’s.
If there were any such law, it would be that singular one about not eating the fruit of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
But that for some thousands of years now is no more—that tree having been removed from the nature of things, or being wholly unknown to us and, like the other creatures of God, granted.
Therefore there is no law according to which Adam’s actual sin is imputed to us.
source_text: Tertium argumentum mihi suppeditant quae sequuntur apud Apostolum: peccatum non imputatur cum lex non est. Atqui lex non est secundum quam nobis imputetur peccatum actuale Adami. Ergo non imputatur nobis. Probo minorem: nam maior est Apostoli. Si qua eiusmodi lex esset, ea esset singularis illa de non edendo fructu arboris scientiae boni & mali. Atqui illa iam ab aliquot annorum millibus non est amplius, sublata e rerum natura illa arbore, aut nobis prorsus ignota, &, ut caeteras Dei creaturas, concessa. Ergo lex non est secundum quam nobis imputetur peccatum actuale Adami.
